summary: Unexpected SSO entityID canonicalization prevents runbook impersonation and blocks on-call login
description:
Issue summary:
Several engineers and on-call SREs are unable to impersonate or log into the internal runbook tool via SSO. Failures began after last week's identity-provider certificate rotation and the Okta attribute normalization migration.

Impact:
- ~8% of on-call authentication attempts return a 403 during impersonation flows; direct login sometimes succeeds but impersonation fails.
- Affects runbook access for new service identities provisioned after the identity migration (accounts created since 2026-03-01).
- Potentially impacts ability to run emergency remediation playbooks.

Environment: prod/us-west region for the runbook-access-proxy cluster. Okta is the IdP with a recent attribute-normalization rollout in front of the SAML exchange.

Steps to reproduce:
1) As a user with runbook-admin role, attempt to impersonate a recently-provisioned service account via console > Runbooks > Impersonate.
2) Observe redirect to Okta SAML assertion and return to runbook-proxy.
3) Runbook-proxy rejects assertion with 403 and logs an entityid mismatch.

Observed logs/snippets:
- runbook-proxy (auth): "SAML assertion audience mismatch: expected 'https://runbooks.internal.redwood.ai/saml', got 'https://runbooks.internal.redwood.ai/' (normalized)"
- okta log: "attributeNormalization: entityID canonicalized from 'https://runbooks.internal.redwood.ai/saml' to 'https://runbooks.internal.redwood.ai/'"
- browser: 403 response body: "ImpersonationDenied: assertion audience not recognized"

Expected behavior:
- runbook-proxy should accept canonicalized forms of the entityID or the IdP should send the expected entityID; impersonation should succeed for valid role-mapped assertions.

Notes:
- Issue is intermittent: legacy identities (pre-2026-03-01) are unaffected. New identities created through the JIT provisioning flow are most commonly failing.
- This appears related to a normalization step that strips the trailing '/saml' suffix in the Okta pipeline; the runbook-proxy strict audience check fails as a result.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:21 - Asha Patel: Ticket opened after Slack #oncall thread reported multiple impersonation failures. Collected sample SAML response and initial runbook-proxy logs.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Marcus Nguyen: Confirmed entityID mismatch error in proxy logs. Temporarily increased debug logging for SAML validation and captured full assertions for three failing accounts.

2026-03-12 13:40 - Identity Platform (Sonia Li): Notified that attribute-normalization rollout completed on 2026-03-01. Looking into canonicalization rules that remove path suffixes. Deployed a rollback candidate to staging last night.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Marcus Nguyen: Reproduced locally against staging Okta and confirmed that Okta normalization rewrites entityID to the canonical host-only form. Created a quick patch to accept either audience in runbook-proxy.

2026-03-14 12:30 - Sonia Li: Identity team will change normalization rules if patch introduces risk; longer-term fix needs coordinated rollout with runbook-proxy.
2026-03-14 15:02 - Marcus Nguyen: Patch PR created: runbook-proxy/pull/742. Requesting review from identity and security for audience-matching logic.

2026-03-14 16:20 - Security (Lina Park): Quick review completed; dual-audience check acceptable as a short-term mitigation with audit logging enabled. Confirmed no increase in accepted unexpected audiences in last 4 hours.
2026-03-14 17:45 - Marcus Nguyen: Monitoring shows impersonation success rate for new identities improved from ~92% failure to ~95% success after mitigation; continuing to watch.
investigation_notes: Collected three SAML assertions and compared 'Audience' values: legacy had '/saml' suffix; new had host-only form.
Hypothesis: Okta normalization pipeline canonicalizes entityID by removing path segments for recently-provisioned apps; runbook-proxy did strict equality check leading to rejection.
Verified that SAML signatures are valid and role attributes are present; only audience mismatch triggers 403.
Staging rollback of normalization confirmed behavior reversal (restores '/saml'). Applying patch should be coordinated to avoid race conditions.
Security review required to ensure dual-audience acceptance does not widen attack surface; audit logs added to proxy to record raw assertion audiences.
Cross-checked with identity provisioning service: JIT creates Okta app link without explicit entityID override, relying on auto-derived metadata which the new normalization changed.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: deployed runbook-proxy patch that accepts both canonicalized and '/saml' audience forms and logs raw audience values for audit. Identity team rolled back the normalization pipeline in lower environments and will coordinate a controlled rollout with updated metadata mapping.

Permanent remediation plan: 1) Update runbook-proxy to perform a robust audience normalization (acceptable host + optional path) with strict validation of signature and issuer. 2) Update identity provisioning templates to include explicit entityID metadata for the runbook app. 3) Create runbook in Confluence documenting coordinated rollout steps with identity and security.

Follow-ups: monitor audit logs for 72 hours, and schedule a postmortem if failure rate exceeds 1% over that window. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbook-proxy/pull/742. Confluence runbook created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runbook+SSO+Integration+Notes
next_steps: Complete security review of audience normalization patch and merge PR #742
Coordinate identity provisioning template update and schedule maintenance window for production metadata update
Monitor impersonation success metrics for 72 hours and report to #identity and #oncall channels
If persistent failures remain, prepare rollback plan for runbook-proxy audience change and escalate to on-call eng manager
